text:
Sylvie: hi all, sylvie here 1st floor, first week on runtime. trying to build from source on Pop!_OS 24.04 (intel+iGPU + nvidia hybrid laptop) with CUDA 11.8 and gcc-12. getting ptxas unsupported PTX and then a cublasLt link missing. any tips?
Sylvie: error:
```
ptxas fatal : ValueError: unsupported PTX version '8.7'
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `cublasLtCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Sylvie: build command: `make -j6 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1` in an env installed via apt + nvidia-driver from system76 PPA
Mika: welcome! hybrid laptops are annoying for this. first check: `nvidia-smi` (should show driver) and `which ptxas`/`ptxas --version`. Also confirm `prime-select` is set to nvidia or use `sudo prime-select nvidia` so the CUDA stack is active for the session.
Sylvie: `nvidia-smi` -> Driver 520.56, shows GPUs: RTX 4060; `which ptxas` -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin/ptxas ; `ptxas --version` -> 10.6.0
Eli: driver 520.x likely doesn't accept PTX 8.7 emitted by some components. Two options: upgrade driver to 525+ or prevent nvcc emitting that PTX by setting `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` to only the SMs of your GPU. For hybrid laptops also ensure nvidia-container-toolkit is configured if you build in docker.
Rosie: also the cublasLt error at link usually means missing `-lcublasLt` or link ordering. Check `ldd` on the object that fails and ensure `/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcublasLt.so` exists.
Sylvie: libcublasLt.so exists. I can't upgrade drivers on this machine (device managed by IT). Is the arch-list workaround safe?
Mika: yes, export `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=\"8.6;8.0;7.5\"` (match 4060 -> 8.6). Or explicitly pass `CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS='-gencode arch=compute_86,code=sm_86'`. That avoids generating newer PTX that the 520 driver rejects.
Eli: for the link: add `-lcublasLt -lcublas -lcudart` to your LDFLAGS or change Makefile link order. Also check if dpkg-installed CUDA stubs are conflicting; sometimes `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` has stub libs that confuse linker order.
Sylvie: tried TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST set to sm_86, build progressed past ptxas but then hit the cublasLt missing symbol during runtime when running tests: `undefined symbol: cublasLtMatmul`
Rosie: that runtime symbol missing indicates host driver/userland mismatch: even if you built older PTX, some cublasLt symbols require driver >=525. On hybrid laptops this is common because system drivers lag. For CI/GPU tests use infra GPU runners or our buildbox.
infra-bot: Recommend dev image: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc12-hybrid-2026-03-20. CI GPU runners: driver 525.85+. See /internal/runbooks/runtime-gpu-runners.md
Sylvie: I mostly want a reproducible dev flow. Is using the runtime-dev docker enough? I remember GPU passthrough still depends on host driver.
Mika: correct. The container standardizes the toolkit for builds but runtime still needs a compatible host driver. For local builds on managed laptops we recommend: (1) use TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST fallback for compile; (2) adjust LDFLAGS for cublasLt; (3) run full GPU tests on buildbox/CI; (4) if you need to iterate on tight GPU-heavy fixes, request temporary buildbox access via infra.
Sylvie: great, that workflow should work. I'll add a short onboarding note with commands I tried (nvcc/ptxas checks, prime-select tip, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST example, and cublasLt link-order) and open a PR to eng-runtime docs. thanks all! :wave:
Mika: welcome aboard Sylvie! ping if you want pairing on the doc.
